findings.passage: “While there is some consolation in the Attorney General’s recognition that this decision has come too close to the April 7 spring election date for implementation in the upcoming election, there is no consolation for the students, senior citizens, low-income, and minority voters who will likely be disenfranchised in future elections because they lack the required state-issued photo I.D. cards.”
findings.note: Press statement after the U.S. Supreme Court declined to review the state photo ID law; she says some voters who lack the required photo ID cards will be disenfranchised.
subjects: effect of photo ID requirement on voters without ID

findings.passage: “Wisconsin’s Voter I.D. law is nothing more than a mean-spirited attempt by Republicans to keep those least favorable to their own candidates away from the polls.”
findings.note: Same 2015 press statement; she describes the voter ID law as an attempt to keep some voters from the polls.

findings.passage: “The current petition process to ensure no eligible citizen is denied the proper ID to vote has clearly been an abject failure,” said Representative Lisa Subeck.
findings.note: Press release on her testimony to the rules committee about extending the emergency rule on the petition process for obtaining a photo ID for voting.
subjects: free state ID / petition process for voters without documents

findings.passage: “It is incumbent upon us as legislators to ensure no eligible voter is disenfranchised by our actions,” said Rep. Subeck.
findings.note: Same 2016 release; she says legislators must make sure eligible voters are not turned away or discouraged from getting ID for voting.
subjects: free state ID / petition process for voters without documents

findings.passage: “Republicans passed their Voter ID law with one goal in mind – to suppress the votes of those least likely to support Republican candidates – and today, they doubled down on that goal,” concluded Rep. Subeck.
findings.note: Same 2016 release; she states a motive for the voter ID law and hopes courts will block it for the November 2016 election.

findings.passage: Instead, we are witnessing them rigging our elections by changing the rules to make it more difficult to cast absentee ballots, making it harder for voters with long-term disabilities to participate in our elections, and removing names from the voter registration lists.
findings.note: Statement on an Assembly vote on several election bills; she objects to absentee ballot rule changes, changes affecting voters with long-term disabilities and removal of names from voter lists.

findings.passage: It is time for Republicans to stop spreading misinformation, acknowledge the fact our elections are safe and secure, and accept the fact President Joe Biden won Wisconsin.”
findings.note: Same 2022 statement; she says the 2020 elections were safe and secure.

findings.passage: We know from court rulings, audits, and recounts that the 2020 election was conducted in a safe, secure, and accurate manner, but Republicans in our government will not stop promoting their baseless accusations that widespread voter fraud swayed the results.
findings.note: Statement on the state Supreme Court decision against unmanned ballot drop boxes; she says the 2020 election was safe and calls voter fraud claims baseless.

findings.passage: “Along with new restrictions that would hinder the efforts of local clerks to help voters cast their ballots, these bills contain provisions that would add barriers for voters who are older or who have medical conditions and are not able to vote in person at their polling place.
findings.note: Joint statement of three Assembly elections committee members, including her, on an election bill package; objects to added barriers for voters who cannot vote in person.

findings.passage: She has introduced Money Out, Voters In legislation to get back money out of politics and the Campaign Integrity Act to ensure accountability, integrity, and transparency in our elections, along with initiatives to ensure every Wisconsinite can exercise safely and securely exercise their right to vote.
findings.note: Campaign site biography text (undated); general line on elections and the right to vote, no mention of ID.

findings.passage: “I can conceive of no legitimate reason that any citizen should need to own or use a semiautomatic assault weapon,” said Rep. Subeck.
findings.note: Release on her circulating a bill for co-sponsors to ban transporting, buying, owning or transferring semiautomatic assault weapons in Wisconsin. She says she sees no legitimate reason for a citizen to own or use one.

findings.passage: “It is time to put people ahead of politics by passing common sense, lifesaving public safety measures such as reinstating the 48 hour waiting period.”
findings.note: Release says she renewed support for reinstating the 48-hour waiting period for handgun purchases and was among legislators circulating a bill to do so.

findings.passage: It is time to pass the Universal Background Check law to require that, no matter what kind of firearm is purchase, or where it is purchased, the process ought to be the same.”
findings.note: Statement after she stood with the governor and other officials to support universal background checks for all firearm purchases.

findings.passage: Universal background checks and extreme risk protection orders have widespread support among Wisconsin residents.
findings.note: Statement backing the governor's call for a special session on universal background checks and extreme risk protection orders.

findings.passage: We cannot accept regular lockdowns and persistent fear of mass shootings as the new normal for children and teachers in our schools.
findings.note: Floor-day statement on a school safety plan. The release (not her words) says the plan included universal background checks, lethal violence protection orders, a 48-hour handgun waiting period and a bump stock ban.

findings.passage: President Biden’s executive action is a vital first step to end senseless gun.
findings.note: Praises the President's April 2021 executive actions. The release lists them (not her words): a rule on kit guns without serial numbers (ghost guns), a rule on stabilizing braces, model red flag legislation for states, and a nominee for the ATF.

findings.passage: "The tragedy at Oxford High School in Michigan underscores the need for guns to be stored safely, locked and out of the hands of children, teens, and those intent to do harm,"
findings.note: Reacts to a hearing on AB 597 (guns in a place of worship on private school grounds). She points to her safe storage package and says she opposes advancing bills that put more guns on school grounds.

findings.passage: We must give law enforcement and the courts the tools they need to protect our families and communities from dangerous individuals with a history of violent behavior.”
findings.note: Release says she authored AB 321/SB 317 to bar firearm access for anyone with a prior domestic violence conviction, including misdemeanor disorderly conduct tied to domestic violence, and called for action on it.
subjects: limits on who may have a gun (domestic violence convictions)

findings.passage: Closing the background check loophole is a common sense measure to prevent felons from getting their hands on firearms in the first place.
findings.note: Statement after an amendment expanding universal background checks was rejected in the Assembly.

findings.passage: Incentivizing the use of trigger locks and gun safes by providing a sales tax exemption is a simple measure we can take to promote safe storage and prevent tragic accidents.”
findings.note: Gun Safe Summer package. The release (not her words) says she co-authored the background check and extreme risk protection order bills and is the Assembly author of the gun safe and trigger lock sales tax exemption.
subjects: sales tax exemption for gun safes

findings.passage: “Ensuring firearms are stored safely, inaccessible to children, and out of the hands of dangerous individuals is just plain common sense.
findings.note: Introducing a five-bill Safe Storage for Gun Safety package (LRB-0699, 0708, 0709, 0710, 0711 per the release).

findings.passage: We must take swift action to close the domestic violence loophole, keeping our families and communities safe by getting guns out of the hands of dangerous individuals with a history of violent behavior.”
findings.note: Statement on the Rahimi ruling. She says state law still lets people convicted of misdemeanor domestic violence crimes keep their guns, and the release says she has introduced a bill to close it.
subjects: limits on who may have a gun (domestic violence convictions)

findings.passage: Exempting gun safes from sales tax encourages safe storage of firearms to prevent accidental shootings and keep our communities safe.
findings.note: Statement when the Ways and Means committee advanced Assembly Bill 10, a sales tax exemption for gun safes.
subjects: sales tax exemption for gun safes

findings.passage: This commonsense legislation takes real, practical steps to keep children safe and prevent tragic, entirely avoidable shootings.”
findings.note: Release says she and a state senator introduced a bill requiring firearms to be locked up or have a locking device engaged when a child lives in or is present in a home.

findings.passage: She has authored bills to prohibit untraceable "ghost guns" and to prevent domestic abusers from having guns.
findings.note: Campaign site home page, under 'Keeping our communities safe'. The page is undated. It also says she introduced Safe Storage for Gun Safety legislation and has worked to close the background check loophole.
subjects: limits on who may have a gun (domestic violence)
